golden_baseline_location: $OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT/parsed/*.psv from a deterministic legacy run of the unit's own namespace (100 pipe-delimited rows for the two-file demo seed: 50 + 50, trailer says 50 each)

acceptance_checks.description: Silver row count equals the legacy .psv row count (100 for the demo seed) and every silver row matches a .psv row on all six fields: cust_id, name, date, amount, currency, record_type.
Amounts are typed as exact decimals (implied-decimal source, integer cents internally), never floats; every amount matches the legacy value to the cent.
Dates are real DATE values; a value the legacy string surgery accepted but which is not a valid calendar date is quarantined, not silently stored.

Per-file trailer count is compared to the parsed record count and a mismatch FAILS the file (the legacy script logged it and moved on); the mismatch is recorded in quarantine with the file name and both counts.
Every rejected record lands in the quarantine table with source file, source line number, the raw line, and a reason code — nothing is dropped silently.

Injecting a letter into an amount field of a fresh drop yields exactly one additional quarantined row with a non-numeric-amount reason and leaves the valid row count otherwise unchanged, while the legacy parser passes the same record.
Re-running the parse over the same bronze input leaves silver and quarantine row counts and contents unchanged.
A run over an empty bronze slice succeeds, writes no rows, and leaves prior silver/quarantine output intact.

planted_anomalies.description: Amount field containing a non-digit character (injected live during the demo) must be quarantined with a non-numeric-amount reason.
A syntactically well-formed but non-existent date (e.g. 20230231) must be quarantined rather than coerced.
A file whose trailer count disagrees with its record count must fail that file and be recorded in quarantine.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: latin-1-safe byte read: decode with a lossless single-byte fallback, never strict UTF-8 decode
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: the raw line stored in quarantine must be the exact source bytes (hex- or base64-safe), so an invalid byte can be inspected after the fact
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: a record containing an undecodable byte is quarantined with an encoding reason; it must never abort the whole run and never be silently repaired

malformed_record_policy.details: Fixed-width slicing is positional: a record whose length or field layout does not match the contract is quarantined (fail-closed). A NULL or missing source value may never fail open into a plausible-looking row — no zero-amount, no epoch date, no empty-string currency substitutions.

empty_input_semantics.details: Empty bronze slice: succeed, write nothing, leave prior silver/quarantine output intact (the legacy chain's 'rerun everything' entry must not be able to erase a day's output).
